question.text: Kavitha and her husband form a young married single-income family with two school-going children and a moderate risk profile. They have Rs. 20,00,000 to invest. Using the moderate-risk young married family model portfolio, how much should be allocated to debt funds?

explanation.text: The Logic: The model portfolio for a young married single-income family with two school-going children (moderate risk) allocates 30% to debt funds. 30% of Rs. 20,00,000 = Rs. 6,00,000. The full source allocation is 35% equity (Rs. 7,00,000), 10% sector (Rs. 2,00,000), 15% gold (Rs. 3,00,000), 30% debt (Rs. 6,00,000) and 10% liquid (Rs. 2,00,000). The Trap: Rs. 7,00,000 (Option D) is the equity allocation (35%), not debt. Rs. 3,00,000 (Option B) is the gold line (15%) and Rs. 2,00,000 (Option A) is either sector or liquid (10% each). Candidates must match each percentage to the asset class named in the question. Note: The stem has been aligned with the source profile (young married single-income family with two school-going kids); using any other profile would give a different allocation table and a different answer.
